en.html:
The enemy armor was brandishing its plaything of a weapon.

What did it take itself for?

A fool?

Functional beauty at one end, this thing at the very other—and you propose to call yourself a full-fledged warrior?

Foolish, foolish, foolish, foolish.

Ugly.
Unclean.

And the arms holding that ridiculous weapon were no improvement.
Of martial technique, not even a trace.

This stance of yours: strength to lift it, strength to bring it down. That is the entire accomplishment.

A child's game of swords.

Even the woodcutter profession would object to being compared with it.

A monkey has learned the use of a stick. There, that is the measure of you.

Incompetent.

And in the sky you will dance about? You have no right.
Go to the bottom of the earth. Let the worms eat you.

Why will you not?

Very well. I will see to it.

I will make you food for the worms.

敵騎が<ruby>玩具<rt>おもちゃ</rt></ruby>のような武器を振りかざしている。

　何だそれは。

　馬鹿か。

　そんな機能美の対極の最果てにある代物を掲げて、
<ruby>一端<rt>いっぱし</rt></ruby>の武者を気取るのか。

　<ruby>愚<rt>おろ</rt></ruby>か愚か愚か愚か。

　醜い。
　<ruby>穢<rt>きたな</rt></ruby>い。

　馬鹿げた武器を構える双腕も同様に愚劣。
　およそ一切の武の<ruby>術技<rt>わざ</rt></ruby>らしきものが無い。

　あれは力で振り上げて力で打ち下ろすだけの<ruby>構<rt>かまえ</rt></ruby>だ。

　子供のちゃんばら遊びだ。

　<ruby>木樵<rt>きこり</rt></ruby>と云えば木樵に失礼だ。

　棒の扱いを覚えた猿、そんなところだ。

　貴様は空に踊る資格など持たない。

　地の底に沈んで虫に食われていればいい。

　何故そうしない。

　そうさせてやる。

　俺が貴様を地虫の餌にする。

en.html:
Look properly.
You fool.

An amateur's weapon—to remove it from his hands is a simple matter.

For an incoming attack, there is more than one way of receiving.
Let the force pass. Absorb it. Do not allow that force to develop in the first place.

Or send it straight back.
In swordsmanship, there is also this receiving form: return a shock the attacker's own hands cannot bear.

You did not know? Of course you did not.
Even this much, this elementary technique.

Battlefield, playground—you ignorant fool have made no distinction.

To a place like this, you came only to play.

And while playing—

————you killed them!!

I squeezed the heat within my body into a narrower space.
Concentrate. Condense. Accelerate. Increase.

Heat gave rise to electricity; electricity took on magnetism.

Uemon-no-jou Muramasa. One Exhaustive-Gathering stroke.
To a blade that was lightning itself, diamond and wastepaper had the same value.

That showy wooden doll, already parted from its weapon—could it stop the stroke even once in ten thousand attempts?

No.
